content:
Plan for Phase 60 — docs/phases/roadmap-parser-decimals-deployed-no-silent-drops.md

Three changes in tagteam/roadmap.py, from defects found running tagteam against Liminal.

1. Decimal phase numbers. `### Phase 9.1:` matches neither _PHASE_HEADING_RE nor
   _PHASE_HEADING_LENIENT_RE, so the phase is invisible to parsing AND to identity
   validation — nothing reports it. Liminal: 28 headings, 26 parsed, silent ~2 months.
   Reproduced against the editable install (repro in the Summary section of the doc).
   Direct sequel to Phase 59, which fixed letters and ruled dotted suffixes out of
   scope as "speculation".
   Fix: widen the suffix group to `((?:\.\d+)?|[A-Za-z]?)` in both heading regexes and
   in _PHASE_NUM_REF_RE / _PHASE_NUM_SLUG_REF_RE.

2. `deployed` is missing from _TERMINAL_STATUS_WORDS, so a deployed phase never leaves
   `roadmap ready`. Verified: is_terminal_status("Deployed to prod") is False.

3. The class defect — silence. A heading that looks like a phase and fails to parse is
   dropped without a word; that is why #1 survived two months and why Phase 59 existed.
   New `unparsed_phase_headings()` returns (line no, line) for `^###[ \t]+Phase\b` lines
   the lenient regex misses; `roadmap check` prints them as `warn:`.

Two points I want reviewed specifically:

- The warning channel must stay OUT of `problems`. validate_identities feeds
  graph_problems -> check_graph, which RAISES RoadmapGraphError on any problem, and
  ready/queue/graph all route through it. Folding the new check into `problems` would
  turn "one phase quietly missing" into "roadmap refused entirely" for any project with
  a stray `### Phase notes` line — strictly worse, and it would fire on upgrade.
  So: separate function, `warn:` lines, exit code unchanged (still 0 on `roadmap ok`).

- Identity needs no logic change. The (number, suffix) pair from Phase 59 already
  handles it: Phase 9 / 9a / 9.1 are (9,""), (9,"a"), (9,".1") — three distinct phases,
  no spurious duplicate. `number` stays int. The only ordering touch is
  sorted(numbers.items()) comparing ".1" vs "a" lexically, which is error-message
  output only.

Explicitly out of scope: multi-level decimals (9.1.2), roman numerals, `9-1`, any
ordering change (number is not a sort key anywhere), any parent/child relationship
between Phase 9 and Phase 9.1, renumbering any roadmap, and `tagteam upgrade` reporting
newly-visible phases.

Rollout, per arbiter decision: ship as a plain bug fix, no flag or migration. Projects
with decimal phases will see those phases appear in ready/queue for the first time —
that goes in the release notes as a behavior change.

Scope of this submission: docs/phases/roadmap-parser-decimals-deployed-no-silent-drops.md
(new) and the Phase 60 entry in docs/roadmap.md. No code changed yet.
Verified: `tagteam roadmap check` -> roadmap ok: 61 phase(s), 18 dependency edge(s);
`tagteam roadmap ready` lists the new phase with its Phase 59 dependency satisfied.

Approved. Reviewed the phase plan against roadmap.py and the existing Phase 59 tests. The four regex changes preserve the existing (number, suffix) identity and document/topological ordering. Adding deployed to the shared terminal predicate covers both scheduling and dependency satisfaction. The separate warning channel is appropriate: unsupported heading syntax should be visible in roadmap check without becoming a new graph error or blocking ready/queue on upgrade. The documented rollout and release-note requirement match the recorded arbiter decision.

Implementation notes within this scope: the listing command is `tagteam roadmap phases`, not `roadmap list` as success criterion 1 says. Emit heading warnings before graph validation can return an error, so unsupported headings are still identified when all headings are unsupported or a separate graph error exists; preserve those existing error exit codes. Cover decimal state-format references, repeated decimal identities, unsupported 9.1.2/9-1 headings and warning line numbers in the focused tests, alongside the listed acceptance cases. The warning guarantee is specifically for suspect lines missed by the lenient regex; it does not cover every strict/lenient formatting discrepancy.

Plan review only; no tests run. The implementation gate remains the one full-suite run.
